title: The verb machine
goal: Master the three groups of present-tense verbs and make sentences negative with the two-part ne … pas.
bekal: form -er, -ir and -re verbs in the present
make a negative with two words wrapped around the verb
recognize that four -er forms sound exactly the same
wave: Go back to **Unit 4** first: order three different drinks with *je voudrais*, then negate each one with *je ne bois pas de…*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Après le cours
dialogs.intro: Thomas asks Budi what he does after class.

lines.speaker: Thomas:
lines.text: Tu travailles ou tu étudies seulement ?
lines.id: Do you work, or do you just study?
lines.literal: you work or you study only?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: J'étudie le jour et je travaille le soir.
lines.id: I study during the day and work in the evening.
lines.literal: I-study the day and I work the evening.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Je finis vers vingt-deux heures. C'est fatigant.
lines.id: I finish around 10 p.m. It's tiring.
lines.literal: I finish toward twenty-two hours. it-is tiring.

lines.speaker: Thomas:
lines.text: Tu ne dors pas beaucoup, alors.
lines.literal: you not sleep not much, then.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Non, je ne dors pas assez. Mais ça va.
lines.id: No, I don't get enough sleep. But it's OK.
lines.literal: no, I not sleep not enough. but that goes.

lines.speaker: Thomas:
lines.id: Do you wait for the bus here?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Oui, mais il n'arrive jamais à l'heure.
lines.id: Yes, but it's never on time.
lines.literal: yes, but it not-arrives never at the-hour.

lines.speaker: Thomas:
lines.text: Je comprends. Moi, je prends le vélo.
lines.id: I get it. Me, I take my bike.
lines.literal: I understand. me, I take the bike.

lines.speaker: Thomas:
lines.text: Non, je n'ai rien. Le vélo, c'est plus simple.
lines.id: No, I don't have anything. A bike is simpler.
lines.literal: no, I not-have nothing. the bike, it-is more simple.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Tu as raison. Je réfléchis à ça aussi.
lines.id: You're right. I'm thinking about that too.
lines.literal: you have reason. I reflect on that too.

notes: **A French negative needs two words.** *Ne* before the verb, *pas* after it. English needs only one ("not"), and learners almost always forget the *pas*. *Je ne travaille* on its own means nothing.
**Before a vowel, ne becomes n'.** *Je n'ai pas*, *il n'arrive pas*, *elle n'étudie pas*. Just like *je → j'* and *le → l'*.

**In conversation, ne often disappears.** French people really do say *je sais pas*, *j'ai pas faim*, *c'est pas grave*. Recognize it when you hear it, but don't copy it in writing — in exams and letters, *ne* is required.

**Ne… jamais, ne… rien.** The other partners of *ne*: *jamais* (never), *rien* (nothing), *personne* (nobody), *plus* (no longer). Only the second word changes; *ne* stays. ⚠️ Don't add *pas* as well: *je n'ai rien*, not *je n'ai pas rien* — just as English says "I have nothing", not "I don't have nothing".
**Étudier ends in -ier** but is still an ordinary -er verb: *j'étudie*, *tu étudies*, *nous étudions*. The only thing to watch is the two vowels in a row in the *nous* form — and both are pronounced.
**Tu as raison** is literally "you have reason" and means "you're right". Its opposite is *tu as tort* (you're wrong). Both use *avoir*, not *être* — just like age in Unit 5.
**À l'heure** = on time. Its relatives: *en avance* (early), *en retard* (late). All three will come in handy right away in Unit 7.

grammars.title: The three verb groups
body: Every French verb ends in -er, -ir or -re. Drop that ending, then add the endings from its column.
after: The **-er** group is the biggest — about nine verbs out of ten. It's also the one that fools your ear most: *parle, parles, parle, parlent* sound **exactly the same**.

The **-ir** verbs that slip in **-iss-** in the three plural forms are the second big group: *finir, choisir, réfléchir, réussir, grandir, rougir*. But careful — many -ir verbs do **not** follow this pattern (*dormir, partir, sortir, venir*), and they have to be learned separately.
The **-re** group is the smallest and the most regular in the singular: the *il* form adds nothing at all (*il attend*, *il répond*, *il vend*).

grammars.title: The rebel -ir verbs
body: A group of -ir verbs that drop their last consonant in the singular. They're very common, so learning them now is cheaper than learning them later.
after: The pattern: the consonant before -ir **disappears** in the three singular forms (dor-mir → *je dors*), then **comes back** in the three plural forms (*nous dormons*).
Other verbs that behave the same way: *servir* (to serve), *mentir* (to lie), *sentir* (to feel, to smell).

grammars.title: Making it negative
body: Two words that always come as a pair wrap around the verb. Only the verb itself sits inside the hug, not the whole sentence.
after: ⚠️ After a negative, *un*, *une*, *du*, *de la*, *des* all shrink to **de**: *j'ai une voiture* → *je n'ai pas **de** voiture*. A rule you met in Unit 4, and one that will keep coming back.
*Le, la, les* don't shrink: *je n'aime pas **le** café*.
If there's a second verb, the pair wraps around **the first verb** only: *je ne veux pas manger*, not *je ne veux manger pas*.

blocks.text: Learn these twenty verbs and their patterns, and you can already build hundreds of sentences. Look at the last letters to tell which group a verb belongs to.

blocks.title: Three sound traps
items: *Il parle* and *ils parlent* sound exactly the same. The only difference is *il* (eel) versus *ils* before a vowel (*ils aiment* = eel-ZEM). Without a vowel, your ear gets no clue at all.
*Je finis* and *il finit* are the same too: fee-NEE. The s and the t at the end are both silent.
*Nous* and *vous* are the two forms that **always** sound different from the rest. If you want to make sure people hear who is doing the action, these two are your friends.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the correct verb form.
Make these sentences negative with ne … pas.
Make these negative using the word in brackets.

items: The bus is never on time.

answers: finis — attends — dort — choisissons — répondez — partent
Je ne travaille pas le soir. — Il ne comprend pas la question. — Nous n'avons pas de voiture. — Tu n'écoutes pas la radio. — Elle n'habite pas à Paris.
Il ne fume jamais. — Je ne mange rien. — Elle ne travaille plus ici. — Je ne vois personne. — Je n'ai pas encore fini.
Je finis vers dix heures. — Il ne dort pas assez. — Je n'ai pas de voiture. — Le bus n'arrive jamais à l'heure. — Nous choisissons un restaurant.
